in what war had neil armstrong served be: Neil Armstrong flew combat missions as a Navy pilot in the Korean War before becoming a test pilot and then an astronaut. In 1969 he became the first person to walk on the Moon.
which is the largest of the so-called te: The terrestrial (rocky) planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, and Earth is the largest, at about 12,742 km across. Venus is only slightly smaller.
what element is the atmosphere of jupite: Jupiter is a gas giant made up mostly of hydrogen, with helium as the next most common gas. Its composition is much closer to the Sun's than to Earth's.
how long does it take saturn to complete: Saturn takes about 29.5 years to circle the Sun once, so a year on Saturn lasts nearly three decades. Its slow trip is why it moves so gradually across our night sky.
the atmosphere of saturn consists mainly: Saturn's atmosphere is mostly hydrogen, with helium making up most of the rest. Like Jupiter, it is a gas giant with no solid surface.
how long does it take neptune to orbit t: Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun. It was discovered in 1846, and it completed its first full orbit since that discovery in 2011.
which of these orders the terrestrial pl: Mercury is the smallest rocky planet, followed by Mars, Venus and Earth. Venus is almost the same size as Earth, but Mars is only about half as wide as Earth.
extraterrestrial life may be closer than: Titan, Saturn's biggest moon, has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane and ethane. Scientists also think it has a hidden water ocean, which is why it is a target in the search for life. Saturn's moon Enceladus is another candidate.
the plot of the 1968 stanley kubrick mov: In the 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey, the spaceship Discovery One travels to Jupiter. The film was based on Arthur C. Clarke's writing, and in his novel the destination is Saturn.
these small bodies are considered left o: Asteroids are rocky and metallic leftovers from the formation of the Solar System about 4.6 billion years ago. Most of them orbit in the belt between Mars and Jupiter.
in 2001, nasa sent this unmanned spacecr: NASA launched Mars Odyssey in 2001, and it has been mapping the planet from orbit ever since. Its instruments found evidence of large amounts of water ice just below the surface.
io and europa are two of the larger sate: Io and Europa are two of Jupiter's four large Galilean moons, along with Ganymede and Callisto. Galileo discovered them in 1610, and Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System.
what is the distinctive feature of the s: The sixth planet from the Sun is Saturn, famous for its bright rings made of billions of pieces of ice and rock. Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune have rings too, but theirs are much fainter.
what was the name of the first spacecraf: Mariner 4 flew past Mars in July 1965 and sent back the first close-up photos of another planet. They showed a cratered, dry world rather than the canals people had imagined.
which one is not a name of a galilean mo: The four Galilean moons of Jupiter are Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto, named after figures from Greek myth linked to Zeus. Athena is a Greek goddess but not one of these moons.
the four jovian planets in the solar sys: The four giant planets are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, while Uranus and Neptune are often called ice giants.
what nasa astronauts made the first unte: In February 1984, Bruce McCandless II and Robert Stewart made the first untethered spacewalks, using a jet-powered backpack called the Manned Maneuvering Unit. It let them float freely away from the Space Shuttle Challenger.
what is the name of the first solar-powe: NASA's Juno spacecraft launched in August 2011 and reached Jupiter in 2016. It is powered by giant solar panels, even though Jupiter is far from the Sun, and it studies the planet's atmosphere and interior.
the lunar seas are actually plains of ga: The dark "seas" on the Moon are huge plains of hardened basaltic lava. Basalt also makes up much of the surface of Mars.
named after the leading sylph in alexand: Ariel is a moon of Uranus, discovered in 1851. Many Uranian moons take their names from characters in the plays of Shakespeare and the poems of Alexander Pope.
what is the fifth largest moon of jupite: Amalthea is a small, reddish moon of Jupiter, discovered in 1892. It is named for the nymph who, in Greek myth, nursed the infant Zeus with goat's milk.
cupid, named after a character in a shak: Cupid is a tiny moon of Uranus, spotted in 2003 in Hubble Space Telescope images. It is named after a character in Shakespeare's play Timon of Athens.
this space object, named after the mytho: Phobos, whose name means "fear" in Greek, is the larger of Mars's two moons and orbits closer to its planet than any other moon in the Solar System. It is slowly spiraling inward, and it may break apart in tens of millions of years.
this constellation is often associated w: Aquarius, the water-bearer, is linked to Ganymede, a Trojan prince Zeus carried off to serve as cupbearer to the gods. Jupiter's largest moon is named after him too.
which of these is the study of mars?: Areology is the study of Mars, from Ares, the Greek god of war and the counterpart of the Roman Mars. Geology is the study of Earth.
which russian astronaut became the first: Russian cosmonaut Yuri Malenchenko married Ekaterina Dmitriev in 2003 while he was aboard the International Space Station. She was on Earth, in Texas, and took part by video link.
this asteroid, orbiting around the sun,: Cruithne is an asteroid that loops around the Sun on a path that keeps it near Earth, which earned it the nickname "Earth's second moon". It is not a true satellite because it does not orbit Earth.
